declarations.explanation: The owner named the licensing: MIT for the code and CC BY 4.0 for the written content (blog posts and other prose), with the copyright notice `Copyright (c) 2026 Jasper Lutz Severino`. The rules allow one root license file only, so the single root LICENSE states both: a header saying which kinds of material each license covers (CC BY 4.0 for the prose the website presents to visitors; MIT for everything else, including source code, configuration, scripts and repository documentation; third-party files under their own notices, such as vendor/ and .agents/skills/, stay under those), then the full MIT License text and the full CC BY 4.0 legal code, each with the owner's copyright notice. No other root license file exists.
evidence: The owner's licensing answer recorded in the earlier v0.20.0 run of this adoption (lutzseverino/site#1): MIT for code, CC BY 4.0 for written content, copyright line `Copyright (c) 2026 Jasper Lutz Severino`; this run restores that LICENSE byte for byte.
The MIT text in LICENSE is byte-identical to the MIT text in the Repo Canon source's own LICENSE (.repo-standards/inputs/source/LICENSE).
The CC BY 4.0 text is the official legal code downloaded unchanged from https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.txt.
The repository root holds LICENSE and no other file matching license.* or license-*; the README structure check's license lookup finds exactly LICENSE.
